title: How many replicas must a read consult?

prereqs.why: The answer is the quorum inequality, and the explanation is why that inequality is the whole mechanism.
There is nothing to choose until the same key lives on several nodes.
Choosing R and W is choosing where on the availability/consistency trade-off you sit, per operation.

statement:
A key-value store keeps every key on **N = 5** replicas. A write is acknowledged to the client once **W = 2** replicas have stored it.

You need the guarantee that **a read always sees the most recently acknowledged write** — no stale values, ever, assuming no replica loses data and enough nodes are reachable.

**What is the smallest number of replicas R that a read must consult?**
hints: Write down what has to be true of the set of W replicas that stored the write and the set of R replicas the read asks. What relationship between those two sets would make a stale read impossible?
Two subsets of a 5-element set are guaranteed to share a member when their sizes add up to more than 5.
Solve R + W > N for R, with N = 5 and W = 2, and remember R has to be a whole number.
